An old, buggy game with outdated game design and ancient-looking textures. The story is barely there, the locations are annoying, and everything feels slow, dragged out, and unnecessarily tedious.

I am not saying the developer did a bad job. It is obvious this was made by a fan, for fans, and I respect that. But for someone who has never played any of these games before, I absolutely cannot recommend it — and here is why.

You can remake the textures in Unreal Engine 5 if you want, but the core design will still be bad. When you spend five minutes searching a location for a rusty pipe made of two polygons that blends into the background just so you can move forward, that is bad design.

When the game makes you run around looking for green buttons, but half of them cannot be pressed because they are just textures, while the actual button you need looks almost the same but is hidden somewhere else — that is bad design too.

The game explains nothing, gives you no clear direction, and constantly feels like it is wasting your time. Some games from 1998 should not be remade. Let them stay dead.

Do not waste your time on this. If you are interested in the world or the story, just watch it on YouTube.

Source Engine. From 2004. Pushed so far beyond its limits that it now struggles to render a hallway at 1080p on hardware that can path-trace Cyberpunk at 4K.

RX 7900 XTX. 64 GB of RAM. This machine can simulate the heat death of the universe in real time. Black Mesa drops to 30 fps when a headcrab explodes.

The Xen chapters are particularly impressive — not because of the art direction, which is genuinely good, but because they somehow make a $1,000 GPU feel like integrated graphics from 2012. HUD post-processing is broken on AMD cards. The audio engine causes frame drops. None of this is fixed. None of this will be fixed.

It took a team of volunteers over a decade to remake a 1998 game, and the final product runs worse than the original running on a Pentium III with a Voodoo 2.

Not recommended. Play the original Half-Life. It respects your hardware.

没有玩过原作《半条命1》，不过重制版的《黑山》还是给我带来了很棒的体验。

《黑山》最大的特点就是没有直接的任务引导。虽然被不少玩家吐槽迷路指引差，但这恰恰是本作的精髓所在。本作完全不依赖UI或任务提示，而是靠空间结构、醒目光效、与环境叙事把玩家自然而然地推向正确路线，这对于有游戏阅历或经验的玩家来说，绝对是非常优秀的设计，极强地增添了代入感和沉浸感。

本作的流程融入了大量的解谜和跳跳乐。跳跳乐暂且不谈，搭配上真实的物理效果解谜绝对是非常有趣的。最让我印象深刻的，当属第9章节的断桥谜题：
“前方断裂的铁平台半悬在水面上，根本无法直接跳跃通行。潜入水里会发现平台下方有一座铁笼，里面摆放着三只红色浮桶，在水下四处搜寻会发现还散落着另外三只。整个流程没有多余提示，依靠游戏真实的浮力物理机制，将所有浮桶都放入笼中，依靠浮力托起铁笼，原本下沉倾斜的平台就会缓缓抬升。”
这处设计把物理交互和关卡解谜融合得恰到好处，十分巧妙，是本作物理解谜魅力的绝佳体现。

NPC 这块真的能看出制作组花了不少心思。无论是科学家还是安保人员的台词都特别丰富，多互动几次就会听到不一样的对话，完全不会单调重复。这种细节做得如此丰富实属少见，这让整个游戏的沉浸感和真实感都上了一个档次。

地图设计也比较巧妙，路线时常曲曲折折，但还能借着管道绕回之前的区域。不过有些看着像是投机取巧的邪道路线，实际上却是真正的主路。这对习惯先把整张地图探索完毕，再继续推进剧情的玩家不算友好，经常走着走着就进入了下一关，想回头都回不去了。

本作的缺点其实也十分明显，整体流程过于冗长，玩久了难免会觉得疲惫。尤其是游戏后期来到 XEN 星之后，关卡流程更是格外拖沓，同样的解谜内容堆好几个。虽说存在刻意延长流程的问题，但它依旧是近期为数不多，能让我静下心来连续沉浸游玩数小时的优秀游戏了。
8.5/10
